requirement:
Node-insertion methods queue selections. They resolve no contents or edges,
render no inputs, and record no observations while building.

Awaiting with a configured agent resolves these selections in call order:

| Insertion | Contents delivered |
| --- | --- |
| `contents_of_current_node()` | The node identified by `ValidationContext::node_id`. |
| `contents_of_successors(label)` | Targets of edges whose labels equal `label`, in returned edge order, including duplicate targets. |

Each successful successor selection records its source, label, and target-set
fingerprint, even when nothing matches. Only selected targets have their contents
resolved. Each delivered node is recorded with its supplied snapshot's
fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.author_procedure`.
Input-resolution failures return `ValidationError::Graph`.
rationale:
The three supplied tests in `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/validation.rs` cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.node_contents`. I did not read the `Memory`, `MockAgent` or renderer helpers. I relied on how the tests use them.

- **Queueing only while building.**
  - `dropped_builders_and_missing_agents_do_not_resolve_queued_inputs` sets `fail_edges` and drops a builder holding both insertions. It asserts that `inspection().dependencies()` is empty. This would catch any edge lookup or observation made at insertion time.
  - The same test awaits without an agent and gets `NoAgentConfigured`. It asserts that `state.reads` and `state.selections` are empty, so nothing was resolved.
  - `queued_reads_selection_and_rendering_fail_before_agent_invocation` drops a `contents_of_current_node()` builder on a configured agent. It asserts that no agent request was made.
  - Rendering at build time cannot be observed separately. Contents are resolved asynchronously, so insertion has nothing to render yet.
- **Call order, current node and repetition.** `explicit_insertions_preserve_order_repetition_and_selection_snapshots` queues current, successors(7), then current. It asserts that the delivered inputs are `[1, 3, 2, 3, 1]` and that `reads` equals `[1,3,2,3,1]`. This shows call order and repeated insertions. It also shows that the current node is `node_id`.
- **Successor selection.**
  - The graph has edges `[(7,3),(8,99),(7,2),(7,3)]`. Delivery is 3, 2, 3, which gives returned edge order, duplicate targets, and filtering by label equality.
  - Node 99 sits behind label 8 and never appears in `reads`. That shows only selected targets are resolved.
- **Selection recording.** The first test asserts `Dependency::OutgoingEdges(1, 7, edge_fingerprint(..))` ahead of the `Node` dependencies. This covers source, label and target-set fingerprint. The `queued_reads...` test loops over empty edges and non-matching edges. It asserts that no reads happen and that the `OutgoingEdges` dependency is still recorded with the empty-set fingerprint. That covers "even when nothing matches".
- **Node fingerprints.** The first test asserts `Dependency::Node(id, fp(content))` for nodes 1, 3 and 2. The node 3 dependency appears once even though node 3 was delivered twice.
- **Failures.** `queued_reads...` injects a read failure, an edges failure and a render failure. Each returns `ValidationError::Graph("read" | "edges" | "render")`. The agent request count stays unchanged. After the render failure, the dependencies are empty.

The obligations stated by the text are all asserted. I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

| Insertion | Contents delivered |

:::{req} author_procedure
`habeas_sdk::procedure` provides a `Send + Sync` per-validation
`ValidationContext<'d, D>` for `D: Domain`, with tracked `inspection(&self)`
and the `ask(&self)` builder under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge`.
Inspection works through shared references. Concurrent calls keep independent
builder, conversation, and submission state, with a shared synchronized trace.
The trace belongs to the enclosing validation.
They require no exclusive context borrow across an agent call and do not
serialize complete interactions behind a context-wide lock.
The trace records the identities and supplied-content fingerprints of inputs
actually delivered, including tool reads. Awaiting with fewer or no node
insertions preserves earlier dependencies; an unawaited builder adds no
agent-delivery dependencies. `Criterion::execute` receives its context under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation.check_procedure`; the domain includes
required evidence storage. This is the same execution interface with or without
agent calls.
